original_question: For magic squares of rank n, determine whether there is any upper limit on n, whether there is a general algorithm for constructing all rank-n magic squares, whether analogous squares can be defined using multiplication or division instead of addition, whether rank-n magic squares can be built from fractional rather than integer entries, and whether there is any meaningful connection between magic-square structure and hadronic or quark charges.
target_in_paper: Section 2.7, "Magic square problem". This paper does not package the target as a numbered conjecture or theorem; the relevant official formulation is the six-part open problem in Section 2.7.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact topic of Section 2.7 and preserves all six components of the paper's open problem: possible upper bound on the rank n, existence of a general construction method for rank-n magic squares, multiplicative and divisive analogues, allowance of fractional entries, and the speculative question about a connection with hadronic/quark charges. It also correctly uses the paper's language of "rank-n" magic squares.
missing_details: The paper first defines a magic square as an array of numbers for which the same number is obtained by adding entries vertically, horizontally, or diagonally; that definition should be stated explicitly.
The paper makes clear by example that "rank-3" means a 3x3 square, so "rank-n" should be made explicit as an n x n array.
Part (i) asks whether there is a limit on the admissible rank n itself, not on the magic constant or on the size of the entries.
Part (ii) is narrower than your draft: it asks for a general algorithm to compose a magic square of arbitrary prescribed rank n, not for an algorithm that enumerates all rank-n magic squares.

The ambient number system is not formally fixed in the paper: the baseline definition only says "numbers," while part (v) contrasts fractional entries with integers. No ring, field, positivity, distinctness, or consecutiveness assumptions are given.

The multiplicative and divisive variants are posed informally. The paper does not define any precise operator convention beyond replacing addition by multiplication, and then asking the same question for division.

Part (vi) is explicitly speculative: it asks for a "plausible linkage" between magic squares and hadronic (quark) charges, and also asks which rank would be the most likely candidate if such a linkage exists.
No extra restrictions such as normal magic squares, use of consecutive integers, uniqueness, classification up to symmetry, or counting formulas appear in the paper and should not be added.

Concepts such as homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency, variables of a polynomial system, or asymptotic quantifiers like "for all sufficiently large m" are not part of this problem and should not be imported into the refined statement.
refined_question: Let a rank-n magic square mean an n x n array of numbers whose row sums, column sums, and two main diagonal sums are all equal. Determine whether there is any upper bound on the possible ranks n for such additive magic squares; whether there exists a general algorithm that constructs a magic square of arbitrary prescribed rank n; whether analogous rank-n squares can be defined by requiring equality of the corresponding row, column, and diagonal values when addition is replaced by multiplication, and separately when it is replaced by division; whether rank-n magic squares may be formed with fractional entries rather than integers; and whether, in the speculative sense intended by the paper, there is any plausible connection between magic-square structure and hadronic (quark) charges, including whether any particular rank n is especially natural for such a connection.
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at Section 2.7 and tracks its six subquestions almost verbatim. The main fixes needed for paper-faithfulness are: (a) restoring the section's own definition of a magic square and the meaning of rank-n via the rank-3 = 3x3 example; (b) narrowing the algorithmic part from constructing all rank-n magic squares to the paper's actual request for a general procedure for arbitrary prescribed rank n; and (c) preserving the speculative wording of the quark-charge item, which asks for a plausible linkage and a likely rank, not a fully formal physical theory. There is no theorem, proposition, or explicitly equivalent reformulation elsewhere in the paper for this item, so the refined question should remain a single sharpened restatement of Section 2.7 itself.
